entries.place: Sacred Grove, Manchester/Palmyra area (approximate witness area)
entries.title: The Father and Son appear to Joseph Smith
entries.desc: In the spring of 1820, fourteen-year-old Joseph Smith went into the woods near his family home to pray. God the Father and Jesus Christ appeared to him. The Father introduced His Beloved Son, and Joseph received an answer to his question about which church to join. The approximate area shown marks where Joseph received the vision; the account does not identify an exact clearing.

entries.place: John Johnson home, Hiram area (approximate witness area)
entries.title: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon behold the Son
entries.desc: While translating the Bible in the John Johnson home at Hiram, Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon pondered John 5:29. Their understanding was opened in a heavenly vision, and they saw the Son at the right hand of the Father. They testified that He lives and learned of the resurrection and the degrees of glory. This pin marks the witnesses’ approximate earthly location, not the heavenly scene.

entries.place: Whitney store, Kirtland area (approximate witness area)
entries.title: A shared vision in the School of the Prophets
entries.desc: The minutes of the School of the Prophets meeting on March 18, 1833, record that many present beheld a heavenly vision of the Savior and angels. The school met in Kirtland, including an upstairs room in the Whitney store. Zebedee Coltrin described an appearance of the Father and Son in a recollection recorded in 1883. Church historians consider that recollection likely connected with this meeting, but its later details and uncertain dating remain distinct from the contemporary minutes.

entries.place: Kirtland Temple, Kirtland area (approximate witness area)
entries.title: Joseph sees the celestial kingdom
entries.desc: On January 21, 1836, while ordinances were being administered in preparation for the Kirtland Temple dedication, Joseph Smith saw the celestial kingdom in vision. He beheld the Father and Son upon the throne and saw his brother Alvin. The Lord taught that those who died without the gospel, but would have received it, could inherit the celestial kingdom. This pin marks the place where Joseph received the vision.

entries.place: Kirtland Temple, Kirtland area (approximate witness area)
entries.title: The Savior accepts the Kirtland Temple
entries.desc: After administering the sacrament on Easter Sunday, Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery prayed behind the veils at the Kirtland Temple pulpit. They saw the Lord, who declared that He lives, forgave their sins, and accepted the house built in His name. Moses, Elias, and Elijah subsequently appeared and committed priesthood keys. The approximate Kirtland pin marks the witnesses’ location.

entries.place: Salt Lake Temple, Salt Lake City area (approximate witness area)
entries.title: Lorenzo Snow testifies of seeing the Savior
entries.scripture: Lorenzo Snow account published by the Church
entries.desc: An account published by the Church recounts Lorenzo Snow’s testimony that Jesus Christ appeared to him in the Salt Lake Temple near the time of President Wilford Woodruff’s death in 1898. His son LeRoi preserved the account, including granddaughter Allie Young Pond’s recollection of what her grandfather told her. President Snow said the Savior instructed him to reorganize the First Presidency without delay. This is an attributed Church history account; the pin marks the temple’s city.

entries.place: Salt Lake City, Utah (approximate witness area)
entries.title: Joseph F. Smith sees the Savior minister to the dead
entries.desc: On October 3, 1918, President Joseph F. Smith pondered the scriptures in Salt Lake City. He saw in vision the righteous dead awaiting deliverance and the Savior ministering among them while His body lay in the tomb. He learned how the Lord organized messengers to carry the gospel to others in the spirit world. The 1918 date belongs to Joseph F. Smith’s vision, not a new earthly visit by Christ. The pin marks the witness’s city, not the location of the spirit world.
